claims: The Rooney Rule is an NFL policy established in 2003.
The Rooney Rule is named after former Steelers owner Dan Rooney.
Originally, the Rooney Rule required interviewing one minority candidate for head coach.
The Rooney Rule now mandates interviewing at least two external minority candidates for head coaching, general manager, and coordinator vacancies.
The definition of diverse candidates now includes women and ethnic minorities.
The Rooney Rule applies to top senior executive jobs.
The Rooney Rule requires at least one minority candidate for QB coach positions.
The NFL rewards teams that develop minority talent who later become head coaches or GMs with enhanced draft picks.
The number of Black head coaches grew from two in 2002 to higher numbers in subsequent years.
In 2026, the Florida Attorney General called the Rooney Rule "unlawful" race-and-sex discrimination.
In 2026, the Florida Attorney General threatened legal action.
Brian Flores is a former Dolphins coach.
Former Dolphins coach Brian Flores brought a lawsuit.
